CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right knee pain after trampoline park injury.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a male who sustained a right knee injury one week ago while jumping on a trampoline at a trampoline park for the first time. He heard a snap and experienced instant pain on the lateral aspect of his right knee upon landing. He reports the pain has persisted for one week. He took acetaminophen for pain relief, which was not helpful. He elevated the knee but did not ice or apply heat. He is able to bear weight but has a slight limp. He denies regular exercise regimen and states he does not work out consistently.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports pain with knee flexion and extension. He denies problems with other joints or systems.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Hypertension
Diabetes mellitus

MEDICATIONS
Lisinopril 20 mg daily (reports taking most days)
Metformin 500 mg (reports taking regularly)

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient went to trampoline park with wife for recreational fun, not exercise. Does not have a consistent exercise regimen. Denies regular workouts.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Blood pressure elevated at 180/80 mmHg.
Heart: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmur appreciated.
Lungs: Clear bilaterally.
Right knee: Tenderness on palpation of the lateral aspect. No tenderness on medial palpation. Able to bend and straighten knee with some limitation. Ecchymosis and edema noted along the lateral aspect. No effusion appreciated. Decent range of motion but pain with some movements. Gait examination reveals a slight limp.

RESULTS
Right knee x-ray: No evidence of fracture or bony abnormality.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Right knee pain - Likely lateral ligament strain. Started meloxicam 15 mg daily for pain and swelling. Referred to physical therapy for strengthening and injury prevention. Further imaging may be considered if pain persists.
2. Hypertension - Continue lisinopril 20 mg daily. Ordered echocardiogram. Medication modification may be needed to better control blood pressure.
3. Diabetes mellitus - Ordered HbA1c to assess long-term blood glucose control. Ordered lipid panel to assess need for medication adjustments. Patient currently checking blood sugars 4-5 times per week; encouraged to check 2-3 times daily.
